Article 2
Letter a The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children victims of acts of violence, constituting respect for human rights and the dignity and honor of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).
Letter b The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair toward men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, and governmental activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter d The principle of the best interests of victims, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e Sufficiently clear

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat of violence, abduction, confinement, falsification of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, entrapment, debt or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of the person holding control or other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes; prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical sexual reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and or body tissue or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d Sufficiently clear Letter e Sufficiently clear

VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Seluma Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Seluma Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency.
6. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others.
21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects.
27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
29. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
30. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 17
Letter a Sufficiently clear Letter b What is meant by basic rights includes the right to obtain education and access to parents during the handling process.
Letter c What is meant by equal protection rights relates to status, citizenship, race, skin color, gender, language, belief, religion, politics or other opinions, ethnicity or social life, property, birth or other status.
Letter d Sufficiently clear Letter e What is meant by the right to obtain freedom is the freedom to express one's views on all matters, including those related to legal processes, care and temporary protection as well as identification and implementation of subsequent solutions.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business world and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Article 13
(1) Regional Government and the community or social service institutions may establish recovery houses or safe houses for victims of violence.
(2) The community or social institutions that establish safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must fulfill the requirements as referred to in the Laws and Regulations.

1.6.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes child marriage prevention as part of community participation obligations: Pasal 7 ayat (2) huruf c states “mencegah terjadinya perkawinan pada usia anak-anak” (prevent marriage at child age). Child/early marriage is commonly treated as a harmful practice affecting girls/children. Since this content is clearly present in the source text and was also retrieved in English, the judge’s “Yes” is supported; the golden “No” appears incorrect for this indicator.

Article 19
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted through:
a. notification of job opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are set forth in the form of an Agreement.
